title: Customer security snapshot — privilege mapping & SIEM ingest notes
content:
Purpose: quick, customer-facing snapshot to explain RBAC v2 role/permission mapping, the audit-log schema we export, and SIEM ingestion options. This is a working doc for customer security reviews and pre-sales technical calls.

Audience: security reviewers, platform engineers on customer side, solutions engineers. Not an SLA; pointers to evidence automation and exports follow.

1) Short summary of RBAC v2 (one-paragraph)
RBAC v2 centralizes authorization into a small set of primitives: Role, Resource, Action, and Scope (tenant, project, route). Roles can be system (admin, infra), org (owner, billing), or app-level (model-deployer, read-only-analytics). Policies are declarative JSON and evaluated at request ingress; policy decisions are logged to audit stream with decision context and policy version ID. Admin UI and API both honor the same policy engine and versioning.

2) Privilege mapping notes (examples customers ask for)
- 'Platform Admin' => can manage org settings, billing, dedicated capacity allocation, and user invite flows.
- 'Model Deployer' => can push model bundles, create model routes, and start/stop dedicated instances for pinned versions.
- 'Read Only' => can view dashboards, logs, and billing data but cannot export credentials or modify policies.
- 'Secrets Operator' (restricted) => rotate API keys and rotate KMS-integrated items but cannot list raw secrets from HSM.

Mapping guidance: provide CSV export of assigned principals per role on request (we generate via admin API). For audit requests, include role assignment event history (who changed membership, timestamp, source IP).

3) Audit log schema (high-level fields)
We export a flattened JSON event per action. Typical fields we include:
- event_id (uuid)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- actor_principal (user/email/service_account)
- actor_id (internal user id)
- action (string e.g., CreateRoute, GenerateToken, PolicyEvaluate)
- target_resource (resource type + id, e.g., model:abc123)
- request_id (trace id correlated with tracing)
- outcome (success|failure|denied)
- reason (free text for failures/denies, policy rule id if applicable)
- decision_policy_version (git sha or semver)
- client_ip
- user_agent
- src_region
- extra (free-form tags: e.g., canary=true)

Sample event (single-line example we provide to customers):
{"event_id": "e5a1...", "timestamp": "2024-10-03T15:24:33Z", "actor_principal": "sally@example.com", "action": "PolicyEvaluate", "target_resource": "policy:rbac/v2/main", "outcome": "success", "decision_policy_version": "v2.3.1", "client_ip": "54.23.3.11"}

Retention notes: Hosted default retention is 90 days for full audit events. For enterprise/private customers we support configurable retention and longer archive exports (S3) on contract.

4) SIEM export patterns and recommended config
Supported export modes:
- Push API (recommended for structured events): Redwood will POST batched JSON to a customer endpoint; supports mutual-TLS and HMAC signatures.
- Syslog (TLS) / Filebeat: for customers that prefer log shipping. We format events as JSON payloads per line.
- Native connector for Splunk/Datadog (enterprise integrations): forwards via secure connector running in customer VPC or via brokered mutual-TLS.

Best practices for ingest:
- Index by event_type and actor_principal.
- Use traced request_id as join key to correlate trace/span data.
- Ingest decision_policy_version for quick rollback/regression queries.

Mapping examples to common fields:
- SIEM_field:user => actor_principal
- SIEM_field:src_ip => client_ip
- SIEM_field:event_type => action
- SIEM_field:outcome => outcome

5) Evidence automation checklist for customer questionnaires
We can produce the following artifacts programmatically for responses:
- RBAC role catalog export (CSV) + current assignments snapshot (CSV)
- Policy definitions and active policy version id (text + sha)
- Audit export for a given date range (ndjson) filtered by actor/resource/action
- SIEM ingestion proof (signed delivery receipt or connector health check logs)
- Config snapshots (retention, KMS key id, TLS cert fingerprint)

How we deliver: use the evidence-automation pipeline (see linked artifact) which runs a job and drops artifacts into a secure S3 share or pushes to an onboarding Jira ticket. Typical turnaround 24-72 hours depending on scope.

6) Common customer Qs + suggested responses (short)
Q: Can you provide proof a specific user was denied access?
A: Yes — provide a filtered audit export for the user/event window with decision outcome and policy_rule_id.

Q: How do you ensure logs are tamper-evident?
A: We sign exports and provide delivery receipts. For Dedicated/Private we can enable append-only S3 buckets and MFA delete.

Q: How do rollouts affect authorization?
A: Policy versioning is atomic; rollouts create a new policy version id and evaluation uses that id. We log both the rollout event and the evaluations tied to that version.

7) Known gaps / tickets (operational transparency)
- Current limitation: we do not yet include session-level KV cache hits in audit events (ticket SEC-512). Roadmap: add lightweight telemetry to help debug cache-related tail latency.
- Export format: customers have asked for CSV-native exports for some event types; we currently deliver NDJSON and CSV via conversion job (SEC-489).

8) Next steps / owners
- Solutions eng to use this snapshot as pre-call one-pager for security reviews (owner: Elliot Wu).
- Security to add a short appendix on KMS/HSM evidence (owner: Maya Patel).
- Engineering to triage SEC-512 and provide ETA (owner: Lars Becker).

Notes / links: see linked artifacts at top for formal design and outstanding Jira tasks. Use this doc to respond to initial customer questionnaire packets; handoff to evidence automation once customer signs NDA/PO.

Draft status: working draft, intended to be slim and practical for pre-sales. Need review from Security and Solutions Eng before marking final.
